title: Hybrid on-the-fly requantization kernel prober and prefill-collapser
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Goal: reduce per-token CPU/GPU overhead introduced by eager dequantization paths and improve throughput for streaming decode and large prefill workloads by introducing (1) a lightweight kernel prober that selects hybrid INT8/FP8 execution per layer/seq-len at request time and (2) a prefill-collapser that fuses KV write and attention precompute to avoid redundant dequant/requant cycles. This ticket scopes design, prototype, perf experiments, and a canary rollout path.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and inference teams
Prototype implements kernel prober that reports latency/cost delta per-layer for INT8 vs FP8 vs mixed paths
Prefill-collapser reduces observed dequant-related memcopies in trace by >=50% for long-prefix prefill workloads
End-to-end P50 latency for decode workloads improves by >=8% on common customer traces without regression on tail latency
Fallback policy ensures functional parity (exact numeric correctness not required) and safe rollback in canary
Telemetry hooks added: per-request kernel-choice, dequant-time, extra memcpy counts, and cache hit rates
notes: 2025-02-12: Kickoff - scoped to decoder-side changes and kernel selection API. Not touching model binary on-disk formats.

2025-02-14: Prototype plan - implement prober as an async sampler that runs during low-percent traffic or in dedicated microbench lanes. Sampler will test a microbatch of requests per model-version and capture wall-time and memcopy counts.

2025-02-16: Trade-off discussion: eager dequant gives simpler kernels and fewer numerical surprises; delayed/on-the-fly requant can amortize memcopies but complicates memory lifetime and KV cache consistency. Decided to implement conservative mode that delays dequant only for ephemeral decode buffers and not for persistent cache entries unless cache-compatibility verified.
2025-02-18: PR stub created for kernel prober interface and telemetry events. Need C++ bindings for async sampler. Linking design doc and early perf dashboard in related_links.

2025-02-20: First microbenchmark shows 12% decode throughput improvement on a 32-token average streaming workload with mixed INT8/FP8 path and prefill fusion enabled on A100-80GB. Tail >=99.9th latency unchanged in lab tests.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design and prober API (2w) - define light-weight sampling contract, telemetry schema, and safety knobs
Phase 2: Prefill-collapser prototype (2w) - implement fusion for KV write + attention precompute on decoder prefill path and avoid intermediate dequant memcpy
Phase 3: Kernel plumbing (1w) - add mixed-precision kernel entrypoints and a requantization trampoline that can be inlined into fused kernels
Phase 4: Benchmarking (1w) - run customer-sim traces, compare P50/P95/P99 and token-cost delta, iterate thresholds
Phase 5: Canary rollout (1w) - enable on <1% traffic with telemetry gating, then ramp to 10% if stable
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: KV cache corruption if delayed requantization writes different byte layout. Mitigation: conservative default keeps cache writes in canonical dequantized fp16 for now; enable requantized cache writes only behind opt-in and additional compatibility tests.
Risk: Numerical quality regressions causing downstream uptime alerts. Mitigation: prober records quality deltas on a holdout eval set and we gate rollout on quality thresholds.
Risk: Increased scheduler complexity and interference with autoscaler. Mitigation: expose a config flag that disables sampling under CPU/GPU pressure and add backpressure hooks.
Risk: Telemetry volume spike. Mitigation: sample telemetry and aggregate histograms on-device before shipping.
